description: An object holding a `value` and pointers to its neighbors (`prev`, `next`). The list is the chain of nodes.
Nodes point both ways, so a node you hold can be removed or moved in O(1) without searching.
The first and last node. Every operation must keep them correct, including when the list becomes empty.
A reference to a node kept elsewhere (in a Map, on a connection object) so the list never has to be searched.
A property the structure always keeps, like 'nodes are ordered by last activity', which makes some queries trivial.
Arrays store elements contiguously, which the CPU reads fast. Linked nodes are scattered, so iteration is slower than Big O suggests.
